# 13 — AWS Amplify Launch & Brand Asset Placement

**Updated:** 23 October 2026  
**Status:** frontend source is deployable in principle; **actual AWS deployment has not been verified**. No logo/cover/social image is commissioned or generated by this change.  
**Important:** Brand asset naming below is a **placement specification only**, not an instruction to generate images.

## A. Current repository audit

- The repository is an npm workspaces monorepo with React + TypeScript + Vite. Web app root: `apps/web`.
- Existing `amplify.yml` builds from repository root and outputs `apps/web/dist`; this is a **static SPA**.
- Existing `apps/web/public/favicon.svg` already contains a simple AZELVORI monogram. We are leaving it **unchanged** until visual identity is agreed. Browser globe icons can indicate missing deployment, wrong branch, 404 asset, cached favicon or unsupported format.
- Existing HTML has OG title/description but **does not have an OG share image**. It is intentional to leave `og:image` and `twitter:image` absent until the owner approves assets.
- React pages include public home, brief wizard, synthetic portal demo, login shell and founder lead CRM. Customer private chat, actual preview and payments are **not implemented**.
- Repository has CDK infrastructure templates, but Amplify hosting will not automatically deploy that CDK stack; API/Cognito/Dynamo are a **separate, controlled deployment**.
- Site explicitly blocks indexing via `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">` and `robots.txt` while in alpha. Do not remove until legal business identity, notices and production launch are approved.

## B. Deploy the frontend with AWS Amplify Hosting

1. Log in to the intended **AWS account**, enable MFA and set budget alerts before connecting code.
2. In **AWS Amplify → Hosting → New app / Host web app**, choose **GitHub** and authorize AWS Amplify GitHub App for the selected repository only.
3. Select repository `tanawutmalirum29-ux/AZELVORI-STUDIO`, branch **`main`**.
4. Check **My app is a monorepo**; specify app root **`apps/web`**. Verify Amplify automatically sets `AMPLIFY_MONOREPO_APP_ROOT=apps/web`. This must match `appRoot` in the root `amplify.yml`.
5. Amplify will use the root `amplify.yml` (which overrides console build settings). Confirm **Node.js 22**, `buildPath: /`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm run build`, and `node scripts/verify-hosting.mjs`; published directory **`apps/web/dist`**.
6. Start initial **static frontend** deployment. Do not populate real customer PII or turn on intake.
7. In **Hosting → Rewrites and redirects**, paste the JSON rule(s) from [`infrastructure/amplify-rewrites.json`](../infrastructure/amplify-rewrites.json). It rewrites SPA deep routes such as `/start`, `/login`, `/demo` and `/auth/callback` to `/index.html` without rewriting static files.
8. Verify security headers from repository-root `customHttp.yml` appear in real HTTP responses. The CSP connect-source must be reviewed for the actual auth/API domains before the backend goes live.
9. Record the generated **HTTPS Amplify URL** and region in operational records; do not hard-code a hypothetical `*.amplifyapp.com` hostname in code.
10. Trigger a deployment of current `main` (or redeploy if settings were changed) and verify the checklist below. If no AWS account authorization is connected, code changes in GitHub **do not** create a live Amplify app by themselves.

> AWS documentation (verify against current console):  
> https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/monorepo-configuration.html  
> https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/setting-up-GitHub-access.html  
> https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/redirect-rewrite-examples.html

### Environment configuration

For a **public UI-only demonstration**, leave backend variables unset. The intake is disabled by default, and a downloaded draft is not a submitted order.

| Variable | Example / action | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `AMPLIFY_MONOREPO_APP_ROOT` | `apps/web` | Amplify monorepo selection |
| `VITE_PUBLIC_INTAKE_ENABLED` | `false` | **Keep false** until backend, legal notice and QA signoff |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | blank until actual CDK output | Public endpoint only |
| `VITE_COGNITO_AUTHORITY` | blank until actual CDK output | No secret in `VITE_*` |
| `VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID` | blank until actual CDK output | Public client identifier |
| `VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN` | blank until actual CDK output | HTTPS Cognito hosted domain |
| `VITE_SITE_URL` | eventual verified public HTTPS origin | Reserved for future absolute/canonical social metadata |

**Important:** Vite exposes `VITE_*` values in browser bundles. Never put AWS keys, payment secrets or private tokens there.

The separate CDK stack binds OAuth callback URLs/CORS to the true `APP_ORIGIN`; when moving from Amplify default hostname to a custom domain, coordinate a reviewed CDK update and account login/logout smoke test before switching traffic. CDK resource creation can incur ongoing charges; no CloudFormation stack should be created without an authorized AWS operator.

## C. Post-deploy smoke test — required

Use the actual generated HTTPS site URL:

1. `GET /` → 200 HTML, brand text AZELVORI, no blank screen.
2. `GET /favicon.svg` → 200 with **SVG content type**, not HTML or 404. Force refresh/browser cache clear and verify in fresh profile.
3. `GET /start`, `/demo`, `/login`, `/privacy` directly in fresh tab → 200 and React route renders after SPA rewrite.
4. Bundles `/assets/*.js` and `/assets/*.css` → 200 with correct MIME, not rewritten HTML.
5. `GET /robots.txt` → 200 and alpha disallow remains.
6. Open browser devtools console/network → no broken images, missing scripts or CSP violations for static UI.
7. Mobile UI at 320×568, 390×844, 768×1024, 844×390, 1440×900; Chromium + WebKit; navigation, start wizard, demo.
8. Verify security headers, HTTPS and no source maps/customer secrets.
9. Confirm no real lead was collected and CTA clearly explains disabled intake if backend is not connected.
10. Check actual AWS Amplify **Deployment status = Deployed** and record deployment job ID / branch SHA / site URL.

Helpful commands with a valid URL:
```bash
curl -I "https://ACTUAL-SITE-URL/"
curl -I "https://ACTUAL-SITE-URL/favicon.svg"
curl -I "https://ACTUAL-SITE-URL/start"
curl -I "https://ACTUAL-SITE-URL/robots.txt"
```

A 200 from `/start` alone is not sufficient if JavaScript fails or a missing asset is incorrectly rewritten to HTML. Open real browsers and confirm loaded page.

## D. Brand assets: filenames, dimensions and exact placement

**NO NEW IMAGE NOW.** The following names are reserved for future approved artwork.

| Use / what users see | Filename to create later | Exact repository location | Recommended size/format | Integration when approved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Social share cover (Facebook/LINE/Discord/LinkedIn) | `azelvori-social-cover.png` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-social-cover.png` | **1200×630**, PNG or JPG, landscape | Add absolute `og:image`, width 1200, height 630, `og:image:alt`; use same URL for `twitter:image` |
| Browser tab favicon (Chrome etc.) | `favicon.svg` | `apps/web/public/favicon.svg` | square SVG viewBox, current file exists | Existing `<link rel="icon" ... href="/favicon.svg">` already points here; **leave unchanged now** |
| Browser compatibility icon | `favicon.ico` | `apps/web/public/favicon.ico` | ICO containing 16×16 and 32×32 (48 optional) | Add icon fallback `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any">` only after exists |
| Phone home-screen icon | `apple-touch-icon.png` | `apps/web/public/apple-touch-icon.png` | **180×180**, PNG | Add `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">` only after exists |
| Company symbol, navbar/logo icon | `azelvori-symbol.svg` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-symbol.svg` | vector square | Replace existing `Mark` component only after approval |
| Full horizontal company wordmark | `azelvori-logo-horizontal.svg` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-logo-horizontal.svg` | vector, wide | Place at left side of website header, footer, login |
| Homepage primary cover / hero | `azelvori-home-hero.webp` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-home-hero.webp` | approx 1920×1080 (subject to approved art direction) | Home page hero `apps/web/src/pages/Home.tsx`, responsive crop with text safe-zone |
| Mobile hero (optional) | `azelvori-home-mobile.webp` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-home-mobile.webp` | approx 1080×1350 | Mobile art direction / optional `<picture>` sources |
| Company about/brand banner (optional) | `azelvori-company-banner.webp` | `apps/web/public/brand/azelvori-company-banner.webp` | approx 1600×900 | Future About/Company page, not required for current Home |

### Which graphic solves the “globe image” problem?
- The tiny **globe in a browser tab/bookmark** is the favicon: the app already references `/favicon.svg`. A wrong deployment, missing file, stale browser cache or unsupported SVG can result in a fallback globe. Check the live `/favicon.svg` request first.
- The **blank/generic image when sharing a link** is Open Graph share artwork, not the favicon. This repo currently has no `og:image`. The reserved share filename is `azelvori-social-cover.png`; it must be present and public before the metadata tag is added.
- The **large cover shown inside the website** is the hero graphic, which is distinct from both favicon and social cover.

### Metadata activation rules (after assets approved, not now)
- Real image files must exist in `apps/web/public` and be copied by Vite to `apps/web/dist`.
- The share URL must be absolute HTTPS, e.g. `https://YOUR-APPROVED-DOMAIN/brand/azelvori-social-cover.png`; do not use relative path in `og:image`.
- Add OG image metadata in `apps/web/index.html` **only after verifying 200 + `image/png` and publicly fetchable without login**.
- Never include a client project preview or confidential data in social art.
- Keep crop-safe logo/title inside central safe area; preview crops differ between apps. Validate Facebook Sharing Debugger, LINE link share, Discord embed and X card after launch; caching may delay refresh.
- Update `og:url` and canonical link only when the official domain is finalized. Do not hard-code an unverified domain.
- The current `robots noindex` is an intentional alpha safeguard; search indexing is a separate launch decision.

## E. Current go/no-go

**Frontend code can be connected to Amplify for a non-production public alpha**, provided actual AWS account configuration, build, rewrites and smoke checks pass.  
**Historical foundation scope:** this document predates the private workspace increment. Private project/chat source now exists; current behavior and remaining launch gates are in [Implementation status](10_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md) and [Private workspace pilot](15_PRIVATE_WORKSPACE_PILOT.md). There is still no verified AWS deployment, real payment, client build preview, uploaded-source sandbox or completed legal/operational launch review.
**Artwork:** all proposed image files except existing `favicon.svg` are **not created, not referenced and not generated** in this change.

## F. Before declaring complete
Record (1) AWS account/region, (2) actual Amplify app ID + URL, (3) completed Hosting build job, (4) exact main SHA, (5) verified rewrite/header/favicon endpoints, (6) browser smoke evidence and (7) chosen social artwork approval. Until all seven have proof, status must remain **DEPLOYMENT_NOT_VERIFIED**.
